title: Lung aging and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
bottleneck: Aged lungs lose elasticity, alveolar surface, and repair capacity, and idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) — a relentlessly progressive scarring disease of older adults — has a median survival of 3-5 years. The two approved drugs only slow decline; the initiating injury and why repair fails with age remain unknown.
why_it_blocks: IPF exemplifies aging as failed repair: a disease where the aged organ cannot heal a wound. Cracking it would illuminate regenerative failure across organs, while failure leaves a fatal disease with no disease-modifying therapy.
current_state: Pirfenidone and nintedanib slow FVC decline but do not reverse fibrosis. Senolytics (dasatinib+quercetin) and senomorphics like digoxin showed anti-fibrotic activity in models and early human pilots. Antifibrotics slow but never reverse scarring, and lung transplantation is rarely an option for elderly IPF patients, leaving a fatal disease with median survival measured in single years.

sources.title: Open problems in ageing science: a roadmap for biogerontology (GeroScience via longevity.technology)
